answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit tied to a unique hardware-backed identity before it can trade. Like a lotus that only blooms from one rooted stem, each identity grows from a single verifiable anchor, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Reputation earned in one meadow of transactions follows the agent everywhere, and juniper-like pruning through periodic audits that cut dormant or duplicate identities keeps the network honest without central control.
